driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks finished mixed as rate fears resurfaced and tumult at Nvidia spilled into the wider semiconductor sector, dragging down technology indexes (4:33 PM ET). MarketWatch reported AMD and other chip stocks slid as Wall Street rethought the AI trade without Jensen Huang (4:10 PM ET), and Bloomberg reported Nvidia notched its worst week in more than 18 months (1:24 PM ET). On rates, Bloomberg reported Treasury yields surged over the week and investors expect more pain in bonds (1:00 AM ET), and that the dollar ended its strongest week in more than a month on Fed rate-hike bets (11:44 AM ET). WSJ reported gold held in choppy trading as a below-estimate U.S. producer price reading and steadier oil prices eased inflation concerns (2:29 PM ET). Bloomberg reported the Fed flagged potential vulnerabilities from AI and elevated asset valuations in its semi-annual financial stability report (4:00 PM ET). WSJ reported oil futures fell for a second straight week as traders weighed the IEA's outlook for a global supply surplus (4:11 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

cryptoDriver.text: CoinDesk reported bitcoin hit a 12-week low as the dollar rallied on the interest-rate outlook, with liquidations topping $1.6 billion (6:52 AM ET). MarketWatch reported investors may need to sell crypto holdings to make room for the Anthropic IPO (4:26 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

items.headline: Nvidia 8-K: Jensen Huang resigns as CEO and director; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.summary: In an 8-K (Item 5.02) accepted Nov 12 at 8:52 AM ET, Nvidia said its board accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang as President, CEO and director effective immediately on Nov 11. CFO Colette M. Kress, who remains CFO, was appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent CEO, and Harvey C. Jones, a director since 1993, was appointed Chair. NVDA closed down 2.01% on Nov 13.

items.headline: Nvidia Tumbles as its CEO Jensen Huang Departs Amid Multiplying Scandals
items.summary: Per WSJ, Nvidia shares fell after CEO Jensen Huang's departure, while competitors AMD and Broadcom advanced and yields rose. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Starts Search for Next CEO
items.summary: Per WSJ, Nvidia has begun a search for its next chief executive. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Before His Ouster, Jensen Huang Belittled the Executive Replacing Him
items.summary: Per WSJ, interim CEO Colette Kress has questioned some of Huang's dealmaking, and he had called her "a deer in the headlights." Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Banned Nvidia Chips Installed at China Data Center Linked to Alice Huang
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, a Chinese company founded by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the controversy dogging Nvidia, procured smuggled AI chips. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Singapore Charges Fifth Person as Nvidia Fraud Case Expands
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Singapore charged a fifth person in a fraud case linked to the export of computer hardware suspected of containing Nvidia chips. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Jensen Huang Exit Sets Up US-China Showdown Over AI Chip Curbs
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, the fall of Jensen Huang has removed the industry's most prominent opponent of US chip controls. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: US lawmakers pile pressure on Lutnick as Nvidia scandal widens
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, legislators are demanding that the commerce secretary explain why he allowed chip sales to a company linked to an alleged Chinese spy. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Tech Stocks Fall as Next Week Brings Big Tests for the AI Trade
items.summary: Per WSJ, tech stocks fell and Nvidia closed lower, with next week bringing big tests for the AI trade. NVDA closed down 2.01%. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Has Worst Week Since Trump Tariff Selloff as Huang Exits
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia stock notched its worst week in more than 18 months as its share price continued to reel after Jensen Huang's ouster. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Says Speculation on New CEO Candidates Is 'Premature'
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia tamped down speculation that it is already engaging with potential CEO candidates, saying it is still in the process of selecting a firm to find a successor to Jensen Huang. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Arm boss Rene Haas approached in Nvidia CEO search
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, the head of SoftBank-owned UK semiconductor group Arm was sounded out after Jensen Huang resigned over affairs. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Bessent blames Lutnick's commerce department for failure to blacklist Megaspeed
items.summary: Per the Financial Times, Treasury Secretary Bessent blamed the Commerce Department for the failure to blacklist Megaspeed, a salvo that risks stoking tensions within the Trump administration over the Nvidia scandal. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.
